page: Microsoft Azure NC144lds_xl_RTXPRO6000BSE_v6 is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine from the NCdsRTXPRO6000BSEv6XL family, designed for compute-heavy workloads requiring dedicated graphics processing. This server features 144 dedicated vCPUs built on the x86_64 architecture using Intel processors, managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is configured with 264.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 1.83 GB per vCPU. The hardware configuration includes a single GPU and a substantial local storage allocation of 7921 GB on NVMe SSDs.

The architectural design of this instance presents a clear tradeoff, prioritizing dense compute capacity and high-speed local storage over system memory capacity. With 144 vCPUs and only 264.0 GB of RAM, it is classified as a low-memory configuration relative to its processing core count. This resource density makes it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that demand massive parallel CPU execution and fast local disk I/O but do not require large in-memory datasets. Appropriate workloads include GPU-accelerated rendering, machine learning inference, video processing, and local database operations that can leverage the 7.9 TB NVMe SSD storage.

This configuration is highly cost-efficient for workloads requiring dense parallel CPU execution and GPU acceleration without requiring large in-memory datasets. It is well-suited for tasks such as GPU-accelerated rendering, machine learning inference, video processing, and local database operations.
